To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the use of baseline data within an individual before data grouping provides a clearer indication of the treatment effects on the gastrointestinal community structure than does an evaluation of data that are grouped by treatment before analysis.

analysis by subject is more effective than analysis of grouped data and that the number of baseline samples and the number of subjects per treatment are important factors to consider when analyzing treatment effects on the gastrointestinal microbiota.
the use of distance coefficients and analysis of individual data are important for the analysis of treatment effects on human intestinal microbiota.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the analysis of the effects of treatments on the microbial ecology in the human intestine.
the effects of dietary intervention on the microbial ecology and the human intestine.
the development of methods for analysis of microbial community structure and how these methods are applied to the analysis of the human intestinal microbiota in two clinical trials.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
analysis of treatment effects on microbial ecology of the gastrointestinal tract should be based on analysis of the data from each individual before grouping by the treatment.
the analysis by subject is the best approach for analyzing treatment effects on gastrointestinal community structure.

the analysis of data by individual before analysis by treatment group is a more reliable and accurate method of assessing treatment effects on the human intestinal microbiota than analysis by treatment group alone.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the best way to analyze treatment effects on the intestinal community is to use a large number of baseline fecal samples from each individual, analyze each subject individually, and then compare treatment effects.
analysis of the data by subject is the most appropriate method for analyzing treatment effects in a human trial.
a large within-subjective sample size is required for a clear analysis of treatment effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is necessary to analyze the data from an individual perspective before performing a group analysis to determine if treatment has had a statistically significant effect.
the analysis of the human gut microbial community should be performed with caution.
the best way to analyze treatment effects is to compare the data from baseline samples to the data from the treatment samples.
